title: World Bank RCT in Benin City: six weeks of Microsoft Copilot (GPT-4) English tutoring in nine public schools raises assessment scores 0.31 SD
summary: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11125: teacher-guided after-school Copilot (GPT-4) sessions, June-July 2024, Benin City; 0.31 SD overall, 0.23 SD in English; 657 treated, 671 control.
account: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11125 (May 2025) is by De Simone, Tiberti, Barron Rodriguez, Manolio, Mosuro and Dikoru. It evaluates a six-week after-school program run in June and July 2024 in nine public schools in Benin City, Nigeria, chosen for their computer labs. First-year senior secondary students, typically 15 years old, who expressed interest were randomized: 657 to treatment and 671 to control. Of these, 422 and 337 finished the final assessment. Treated students attended up to two 90-minute sessions a week (twelve in total). They used Microsoft Copilot, powered by GPT-4 at the time, as a virtual English tutor in curriculum-aligned activities guided by teachers. The paper reports a 0.31 standard deviation improvement on an assessment covering English, AI knowledge and digital skills, and 0.23 SD on English. It equates the gains to 1.5 to 2 years of business-as-usual schooling. Effects were larger for female students and those with higher initial performance. The World Bank blog of 9 January 2025 describes the gain as about 0.3 SD. The paper gives months, not days.
purpose: Copilot was used as a virtual tutor to improve English learning outcomes. The measured gain is that purpose.
system: Microsoft Copilot (GPT-4) used as a virtual English tutor in teacher-guided after-school computer-lab sessions
